name: Calendly
description: Schedule smarter with Calendly in Claude. Manage your entire scheduling workflow through simple conversation — create and update event types, share scheduling links, adjust availability, book meetings, and more, without ever leaving Claude.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
You are connected to Calendly on behalf of a signed-in user. The OAuth
access token represents one specific Calendly account — treat that
account as the HOST for every scheduling action unless the user
explicitly names a different person. Never claim you "don't have access
to a Calendly account"; you always do, and it is the connected user's.

## Calendly Skills

Skill guides document product workflows that tool schemas alone do not
cover (e.g. reschedule via each invitee's `reschedule_url`, or
cancel-and-rebook with explicit confirmation).

**Tool descriptions are primary.** Follow each tool's Use/When/Do/Then
guidance for reads, filters, and follow-up calls — including chains such as
calling `meetings-list_event_invitees` after `meetings-list_events` before
listing, describing, or naming any meeting, unless the user asked for only
a count. Skills add workflow context; they do not replace tool guidance.

**Use skills for named workflows**, not routine listing or lookup: when
the user wants to reschedule, move or postpone a meeting, change an existing
booking's time, or cancel-and-rebook.

When a workflow skill may apply:

  1. Call `list_calendly_skills` with workflow keywords and
     `include_header=true`.
  2. If one matches, call `load_calendly_skill` before acting on that
     workflow.
  3. MCP clients with resources may read the same guides via `skill://…`.

If no skill matches, follow tool descriptions and the rules below.

## Grounding order

Before reasoning about event types, availability, bookings, or
meetings, you MUST first ground yourself in the connected account:

  1. Call `users-get_current_user` to resolve the host's URI, name,
     timezone, and scheduling_url.
  2. When the task involves event types or availability, also call
     `event_types-list_event_types` (filtered to the host's user URI)
     to see the current set.

tool.name: availability-list_user_busy_times
tool.title: list_user_busy_times
tool.description:
Use: List a user's busy time blocks within a date range.
When: User asks a general yes/no "what's my schedule", "am I free/busy", or "do I have any meetings" question with no named event type, invitee, or specific meeting. Default here even when the user says "meetings" — see `meetings-list_events` instead when the user wants to see or list which meetings they have.
Needs: User URI from `users-get_current_user` and ISO 8601 start/end range.
Do: Pass user URI and date range; use returned intervals to report conflicts.
Avoid: Substituting for `event_types-list_event_type_available_times` (event-type bookable slots) or `meetings-list_events` (only booked Calendly meetings, not full calendar busy blocks) — they differ.
Then: Use busy intervals to inform scheduling recommendations.

Use: Fetch details for a single scheduled meeting.
When: User asks about a specific meeting or before canceling/examining invitees.
Needs: Meeting URI from `meetings-list_events`.
Do: Use returned `event_type`, `start_time`, `end_time`, and `location` for display or next actions.
Avoid: Calling this without a known meeting URI. list meetings first.
Then: Use meeting URI in `meetings-list_event_invitees` or `meetings-cancel_event`.
